slots.practicalActivity: Ask a real LLM you have access to a question about something recent (post-cutoff) and a question about a fictional internal document you make up, and record whether it hallucinates confident specifics instead of admitting it doesn't know.
slots.deliverable: A short write-up of the two real LLM responses with every hallucinated specific marked.

slots.practicalActivity: List 3 real facts about a business (real or hypothetical) that change at least monthly and 1 behavior/tone requirement that wouldn't change often, then apply the lesson's decision rule to each.
slots.deliverable: A decision table mapping each of the 4 items to RAG or fine-tuning, with one sentence of reasoning per row.

slots.practicalActivity: From memory, sketch the five query-time RAG steps in order, then annotate each step with one specific thing that could go wrong there.
slots.deliverable: A 5-step pipeline diagram with a real, specific failure mode noted at each step.

lessons.title: When RAG Is the Wrong Answer

slots.practicalActivity: Run 3 real or hypothetical LLM feature ideas through the lesson's 4-question RAG-fit checklist and decide honestly whether each needs RAG, a prompt, a fine-tune, or a tool call.
slots.deliverable: A written verdict for all 3 ideas with the checklist answers justifying each decision.

slots.practicalActivity: Call a real embedding API (e.g. OpenAI's text-embedding-3-small) on 3 original phrases you write — two paraphrases of the same idea and one unrelated phrase — and compute the real cosine similarity between each pair.
slots.deliverable: Printed real embedding similarity scores for the 3 phrase pairs, confirming the paraphrase pair scores noticeably higher than the unrelated pair.

slots.practicalActivity: Look up the current real MTEB retrieval leaderboard, record the top hosted and top self-hosted model you find, and write one concrete trade-off between the two categories for a project you choose.
slots.deliverable: A short written comparison naming a real hosted and a real self-hosted embedding model with one concrete trade-off between them.

lessons.title: Similarity Metrics: Cosine, Dot Product & Euclidean

slots.practicalActivity: By hand, compute the cosine similarity and dot product for two real 3-dimensional vectors you choose, then L2-normalize both vectors and recompute the dot product to confirm it now matches the cosine similarity.
slots.deliverable: A worked calculation sheet showing all three metrics plus the confirmed normalization check.

slots.practicalActivity: Using the dims x 4 bytes formula, calculate the real raw storage cost for 500,000 chunks at 384, 768, and 1536 dimensions, then write one paragraph on when you'd accept the larger cost.
slots.deliverable: A table of 3 real storage-cost calculations plus a one-paragraph recommendation.

slots.practicalActivity: Draft 5 real questions a target knowledge base's users would ask, name which document should answer each, and apply the lesson's shortlist process against one real hard constraint (e.g. data residency or budget).
slots.deliverable: A 5-question evaluation seed set plus a one-paragraph model shortlist decision grounded in a real constraint.

slots.practicalActivity: Sign up for a free Qdrant Cloud cluster (or run Qdrant locally via Docker), run a real create-collection call with a chosen distance metric, then upsert and query a handful of real vectors using all four core operations.
slots.deliverable: Captured real console or terminal output showing a created collection and a successful query response.

slots.practicalActivity: Compare Pinecone, Qdrant, Weaviate, Chroma, and Milvus against a real project's requirements (self-hosted vs. managed, hybrid search, scale), then pick one for a solo weekend prototype and a different one for a production pipeline, with written justification for each.
slots.deliverable: A written comparison table of the 5 databases with a final pick and justification for both scenarios.

slots.practicalActivity: Using the lesson's real IVF math, calculate how many vectors land per cluster for nlist=2,000 over 4,000,000 vectors, then if you have a real vector database running, tune its nprobe or ef parameter and observe the real recall-versus-speed change.
slots.deliverable: Worked IVF cluster-size calculations plus, if run locally, a recorded recall-vs-speed trade-off at two different parameter settings.

slots.practicalActivity: Write a real metadata filter (must/should/must_not, in the style shown in the lesson) scoping a search to a specific tenant_id and a date range, then run it against real upserted test data in your vector database and confirm it excludes the right records.
slots.deliverable: A working filter query plus real query results confirming correct inclusion and exclusion.

slots.practicalActivity: Compute a real Reciprocal Rank Fusion score by hand (k=60) for two documents ranked differently in a dense list and a sparse list, following the lesson's worked example, and confirm which document the fused ranking favors and why.
slots.deliverable: A worked RRF calculation table showing the real fused ranking and a one-sentence explanation of the result.

slots.practicalActivity: Using Qdrant's real RAM formula (vectors x dims x 4 bytes x 1.5), estimate the memory footprint for 3 different real collection sizes/dimensionalities, then decide for each whether vertical or horizontal scaling fits better.
slots.deliverable: 3 worked RAM-sizing calculations with a scaling recommendation for each.

slots.practicalActivity: Chapter wrap lab: stand up a real vector database (Chroma locally or Qdrant free tier), create a collection with your chosen distance metric and dimensionality, upsert at least 20 real embedded chunks with metadata, then run both a filtered query and a hybrid query against it.
slots.deliverable: A working notebook or script showing a real created collection, 20+ upserted vectors, and both a filtered and a hybrid query returning real results.

slots.practicalActivity: Run LangChain's real RecursiveCharacterTextSplitter (chunk_size=500, chunk_overlap=50) on an actual multi-paragraph document you choose, and inspect the real resulting chunks for sentence-boundary preservation.
slots.deliverable: The real list of generated chunks with character counts, annotated for any boundary issues found.

slots.practicalActivity: Chunk the same real document once at roughly 100 tokens and once at roughly 400 tokens, compare which version better answers a narrow factual question versus a broad how-does-this-work question, and propose a paired top_k for each chunk size.
slots.deliverable: A side-by-side comparison of the two chunkings' outputs with a top_k recommendation for each.

slots.practicalActivity: Send a real search request (vector, limit, with_payload, score_threshold) against your populated vector database collection from the Chapter 3 lab, and inspect the real scored, payload-bearing response.
slots.deliverable: A captured real request/response pair from your own vector database search.

slots.practicalActivity: Take the top 20 real candidates from your retrieval step and run them through a real re-ranking API (Cohere's Rerank free tier) to get a reordered top-5 by relevance_score.
slots.deliverable: A real before/after ranking comparison showing vector-search order versus re-ranked order for the same query.

slots.practicalActivity: Assemble a real Messages API call with a grounding system instruction and your own numbered, re-ranked chunks in the user turn, send it, and capture the real model response.
slots.deliverable: The real assembled request JSON plus the real grounded answer it produced.

slots.practicalActivity: Implement the manual bracket-number citation mapping (regex extracting [n] and resolving it to chunk metadata) against a real model answer from the previous slot, then try the Messages API's built-in document citations on the same chunks and compare the two outputs.
slots.deliverable: A working citation-resolution script plus a side-by-side comparison of manual vs. built-in citation output on the same real answer.

slots.practicalActivity: Add a real score_threshold abstention check to your pipeline, then test it with 3 real queries — one clearly in-scope, one clearly out-of-scope, and one ambiguous — confirming the pipeline abstains correctly on the out-of-scope case.
slots.deliverable: Real pipeline output for all 3 test queries, including a confirmed abstention on the out-of-scope one.

slots.practicalActivity: Chapter wrap lab: wire ingestion, retrieval, re-ranking, grounded prompt assembly, citations, and the abstention check into one real callable answer_question function, following the course's Lesson 29 pattern, and run it end to end on 3 real questions against your own knowledge base.
slots.deliverable: One working answer_question function plus real, captured output (including citations) for 3 end-to-end test questions.

slots.practicalActivity: Have a real LLM generate 3 reformulated phrasings of a terse test question, run retrieval for each against your vector database, and deduplicate the combined results by chunk ID.
slots.deliverable: The real 3 reformulated queries plus the deduplicated combined retrieval result set.

slots.practicalActivity: Generate a real hypothetical-answer paragraph for a test question using an LLM call, embed it, and compare its retrieval results against embedding the original terse question directly.
slots.deliverable: A side-by-side comparison of real retrieval results from the question-embedding approach versus the HyDE approach for the same test question.

slots.practicalActivity: Define a real search_knowledge_base tool schema and wire it into a tool-calling loop so the model decides when to call retrieval, then test it on a multi-part question that should trigger two separate real searches.
slots.deliverable: A real transcript showing the model calling search_knowledge_base twice with two different queries before answering.

slots.practicalActivity: Write a real Cypher-style query (on paper, or against a free Neo4j Aura sandbox) answering a relational question your own knowledge base's documents would raise, then explain why vector search alone couldn't answer it.
slots.deliverable: A written or executed Cypher query plus an explanation of the relational question it answers that vector search can't.

slots.practicalActivity: Build a small Ragas evaluation set (at least 5 real question/retrieved-context/response/reference rows from your own pipeline's real output, including one honest 'I don't know' case) and run Faithfulness and LLMContextRecall against it.
slots.deliverable: Real Ragas evaluation scores for faithfulness and context recall across your 5+ row test set.

slots.practicalActivity: Choose your own real knowledge base (a set of policy, support, or product documents) for the capstone, and write out the lesson's 8-item done-checklist as your own project plan, mapping each item to a specific real document source.
slots.deliverable: A written capstone project plan with the 8-item done-checklist adapted to your chosen real documents.

lessons.title: Capstone: Building a Production RAG Knowledge Assistant

slots.practicalActivity: Build the real answer_question pipeline function (embed, search with score_threshold, rerank, assemble a grounded prompt with citations) against your chosen capstone knowledge base, and run it on a real end-to-end question.
slots.deliverable: A working capstone pipeline producing one real, cited, grounded answer end to end.

slots.practicalActivity: Build a real 10+ question evaluation set for your capstone (including an honest 'I don't know' case), run a real Ragas evaluation, identify the lowest-scoring metric, make one measured tuning change (e.g. raise top_k), and re-run the same evaluation to confirm improvement.
slots.deliverable: Real before/after Ragas scores proving a specific tuning change measurably improved the targeted metric.

slots.practicalActivity: Write the capstone's portfolio README covering the architecture, the real before/after evaluation numbers, and a demonstrated abstention case, then rehearse explaining the project's 'sentence that ties it together' out loud.
slots.deliverable: A README.md portfolio writeup containing real architecture notes and the real before/after evaluation numbers from the capstone.

monthlyMilestoneContribution: After finishing this course, a student can design and build a real retrieval-augmented generation pipeline end to end — choosing and evaluating embedding models, standing up and querying a real vector database, chunking and retrieving with re-ranking and citations, and measuring and tuning retrieval quality with Ragas — culminating in a working, evaluated, cited RAG knowledge assistant.
